lines.cap: This royal family kept it in the family for so long, their last king couldn't even chew his food.
lines.say: This royal family kept it in the family for so long, their last king couldn't even chew his food.

lines.cap: The Habsburgs. For six hundred years they ruled Spain, Austria, and half of Europe.
lines.say: The Habsburgs. For six hundred years they ruled Spain, Austria, and half of Europe.

lines.cap: To keep the power in the family, they married each other. Uncles married nieces. Cousins married cousins. Again and again.
lines.say: To keep the power in the family, they married each other. Uncles married nieces. Cousins married cousins. Again and again.

lines.cap: The result was a famous jaw. Huge, jutting, and passed down for generations. You can see it in their portraits.
lines.say: The result was a famous jaw. Huge, jutting, and passed down for generations. You can see it in their portraits.

lines.cap: Then came Charles the Second of Spain. His jaw was so big, he struggled to chew and speak. He had no children.
lines.say: Then came Charles the Second of Spain. His jaw was so big, he struggled to chew and speak. He had no children.

lines.cap: When he died in 1700, the Spanish Habsburgs ended, and a thirteen year war broke out over his throne.
lines.say: When he died in 1700, the Spanish Habsburgs ended, and a thirteen year war broke out over his throne.

lines.cap: Modern scientists studied his family tree. It was less of a tree. More of a wreath.
lines.say: Modern scientists studied his family tree. It was less of a tree. More of a wreath.
